content.text: No exclusivity binding PB exists; the only exclusivity commitment runs against SFJ and benefits us.

input.quote: 3.19 Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ. During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
input.rationale: The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement is Section 3.19, which binds SFJ (and its Affiliates) not to trial or sell Competing Products during the Exclusive Period (ending November 21, 2022 / November 21, 2024 per Section 1.1.68). That restriction runs in PB's favour and, per the detection guidance, exclusivity granted to Customer is acceptable and is not flagged. We found no reciprocal covenant requiring PB to source, purchase or procure exclusively from SFJ, no "sole supplier" language, and no bar on PB engaging third parties for supply — indeed PB is itself the GMP Manufacturer and supplier of Product under Section 3.14.1. The Section 7.5 negative covenants (indebtedness, liens, distributions and the Section 7.5.5 consent right over non-Excluded Licensing Transactions) are financing-style restrictions tied to SFJ's security interest and an out-licensing consent mechanic; they are not a sourcing or sole-supplier obligation and fall outside this rule's boundary (they are noted here only for completeness). The clause set therefore meets the preferred position — PB carries no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation — so no redline is proposed.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
